nodes.label: Admin Role Kind
nodes.rationale: Admin roles hold only admin keys because a staff permission is unusable to a user whose navigation is confined to the admin routes.

nodes.label: Mirrored Admin and Staff Data Routes
nodes.norm_label: mirrored admin and staff data routes
nodes.rationale: Kept as separate routes rather than one route branching on permissions, because the admin table has features the staff table does not and merging them would tangle two interfaces.

nodes.label: Open: Staff Module Actions Beyond View
nodes.norm_label: open: staff module actions beyond view
nodes.rationale: Blocked on deciding whether encoder-submitted data needs approval before it counts toward reports.

nodes.label: Check Permission Keys, Never Role Names
nodes.norm_label: check permission keys, never role names
nodes.rationale: Role names are runtime data an admin can rename, while keys are defined in source and cannot change underneath the code.

nodes.label: User to Role to Permission Model
nodes.norm_label: user to role to permission model
nodes.rationale: One role per user with no per-user overrides; a person needing a different set gets a duplicated role instead.

nodes.label: Admin Template
nodes.rationale: Derived by filtering rather than listed by hand, so a new admin page is picked up automatically while the Roles page stays excluded.

nodes.label: Bootstrap via create-admin
nodes.rationale: Finds the super-admin role by permission rather than by name, creating it from the template only when none exists.

nodes.label: Role Templates
nodes.rationale: Pre-checked defaults only; never saved as records, so a created role keeps no connection to the template it came from.

nodes.label: Super Admin Template
nodes.rationale: The only template including the Roles page keys, and what the bootstrap script reads on a fresh server.

nodes.label: Commit Primary Changes Scope
nodes.rationale: Stages only the files created or modified while completing the current session's task, named one by one instead of git add -A. When the session holds no completed task the files may have changed for reasons never observed, so the correct move is to ask which files are primary rather than guess.

nodes.label: Commit Staged Files Scope
nodes.rationale: Commits exactly the existing index, read with git diff --cached --name-only, and stages nothing new. When the index is empty the run stops and says so rather than guessing at something to add.

nodes.label: Commit This Scope
nodes.rationale: The default when no scope is named: git add -A sweeps modified, deleted, and untracked files. Whatever got swept in that is not the main work is called out in the trailing bullet, and a file that should not be in the repo at all is named and left out rather than committed quietly.

nodes.label: Pre-Commit Format Check
nodes.rationale: A closing checklist re-verifies the staging scope, the prefix and lowercase title, the blank line after it, main-before-unrelated ordering, a bullet or two-space wrap on every body line, the 72-character limit, and the absence of trailers.

nodes.label: No Commit Trailers
nodes.rationale: No Co-Authored-By trailer and no generated-with footer are permitted anywhere in the message.

nodes.label: Bullet Body
nodes.rationale: The body is bullets only, wrapped at 72 characters with two-space continuation indents, one bullet per logical change, three to six bullets in total. Identifiers are written out literally. A commit that needs more than six bullets is probably doing too much and should be split.

nodes.label: Commit Message Format
nodes.rationale: The repo enforces one house shape for commit messages so history stays scannable: a conventional prefix and short lowercase title, a blank line, then a wrapped bullet list. Prose paragraphs are rejected because they bury several logical changes in one block.

nodes.label: Conventional Prefix Title
nodes.rationale: The title takes a conventional prefix (feat, fix, refactor, chore, docs, test), a lowercase first letter, no trailing period, and stays under about 72 characters. Previously untracked files are feat rather than refactor, because nothing existed yet to refactor.

nodes.label: Default Body Ordering
nodes.rationale: Main changes come first, most important first, then anything swept into the same commit that is not part of that work. Trailing bullets stay short; an unrelated change big enough to need its own explanation belongs in its own commit instead.

nodes.label: Staging Scope
nodes.rationale: Which files get staged is settled before the message is written, because the wrong scope forces an amend or a reset afterwards. Three phrases select the scope and the widest one is also the default; the scope is never widened on the agent's own initiative.

nodes.label: Expand Permissions Walks the Whole Chain
nodes.norm_label: expand permissions walks the whole chain
nodes.rationale: PERMISSION_IMPLIES stores single steps only, and expansion is idempotent, so it is safe to apply anywhere.

nodes.label: Implied Permissions
nodes.rationale: Unrecognised keys pass through untouched rather than being dropped, so a leftover database row never silently removes access it was already granting.

nodes.label: Open: Orphan Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Orphans are removed by hand today; whether the sync script should offer deletion is undecided and not urgent.

nodes.label: Orphan Keys Reported, Never Deleted
nodes.rationale: The join table is declared without a delete cascade, so MySQL restricts the delete; clearing an orphan means removing live role grants first, which is not a decision a script should make unattended.

nodes.label: Permission Sync
nodes.rationale: Permission rows are data, not schema, so the migration generator produces nothing for a new key and this script is what puts it into the database.

nodes.label: RBAC Locked Decisions
nodes.rationale: Written as locked decisions so permission work does not re-litigate settled design each time it is touched.

nodes.label: Roles Page Keys Hidden From the Editor
nodes.norm_label: roles page keys hidden from the editor
nodes.rationale: Absent rather than greyed out, so no admin can grant the restricted key through the interface at all.

nodes.label: Keys Built Forward, Never Split Apart
nodes.norm_label: keys built forward, never split apart
nodes.rationale: The underscore is both the separator and a legal character inside a submodule name, so a finished key cannot be parsed back into its parts unambiguously.

nodes.label: Mandatory View Action Per Module
nodes.rationale: Each route load function checks the module view key, so a module without one is unreachable by anybody.

nodes.label: One Level of Submodules
nodes.rationale: Deeper nesting would make the action-first flattening ambiguous.

nodes.label: Open: Surfacing Role Contents Outside the Roles Page
nodes.norm_label: open: surfacing role contents outside the roles page
nodes.rationale: A user manager assigns roles by name alone; a popover listing the selected role permissions is the likely fix.

nodes.label: Permission Key Shape
nodes.rationale: PERMISSION_DEFS is the single source, so a new module or action is added in exactly one place.

nodes.label: Roles Editor Is Super-Admin Only
nodes.rationale: View is withheld alongside manage because a Roles page nobody can edit has no reason to exist, so the read-only rendering is never built.

nodes.label: Exactly One Holder of the Restricted Key
nodes.norm_label: exactly one holder of the restricted key
nodes.rationale: Enforced as a safety net against a bypassed request, since the interface already makes the key unreachable.

nodes.label: Role Editor Auto-Tick
nodes.rationale: Managing a page you cannot open is meaningless, so any non-view action ticks its module view, and unticking view clears the module.

nodes.label: Server-Side Expansion Before Writing
nodes.rationale: The browser can be bypassed, so expanding on the server means the database can never reach a state the interface would not have produced.

nodes.label: Primary and Foreign Key Naming
nodes.rationale: Semantic foreign key names are allowed where the name does not match the referenced table, documented inline in the schema file.

nodes.label: Snake Case Columns, Camel Case Fields
nodes.norm_label: snake case columns, camel case fields
nodes.rationale: Mapped in the Drizzle schema so the database and TypeScript each keep their own convention.

nodes.label: Soft Delete via Status Enum
nodes.rationale: A status enum rather than a boolean flag, so more than two lifecycle states stay expressible.

nodes.label: Frozen Super-Admin Role
nodes.rationale: Only the description is editable; name, status, and the permission set are locked, and deletion, deactivation, and duplication are blocked.

nodes.label: Never Zero Active Super-Admins
nodes.rationale: Any action dropping the count to zero is blocked; going from two down to one warns but is allowed.

nodes.label: Protection From a Live Condition, Not a Column
nodes.norm_label: protection from a live condition, not a column
nodes.rationale: There is no protection flag column; protection is derived by asking whether the role currently holds the roles-management key.

nodes.label: No User Changes Their Own Role
nodes.norm_label: no user changes their own role
nodes.rationale: Prevents both self-promotion and self-lockout, where an admin strips their own access to the only page that could undo it.

nodes.label: Only a Super-Admin Assigns Super-Admin
nodes.rationale: Together with the self-change rule this closes the grant path: a user manager can neither promote themselves nor a colleague, and unassignment is restricted the same way.

nodes.label: Super-Admin Backfill
nodes.rationale: Required because the frozen role has no interface path to gain a new module.

nodes.label: Super-Admin Role
nodes.rationale: Identified by holding the roles-management key rather than by name, since names are editable runtime data.

nodes.label: DENR Agency Logo (Department of Environment and Natural Resources)
nodes.norm_label: denr agency logo (department of environment and natural resources)

nodes.label: create-admin.ts two-insert bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Inserts the employee row first, then the login pointing at it, both in one transaction so a taken username does not leave an orphan employee when the prompt retries.

nodes.label: endSessionsForEmployee
nodes.rationale: Shared helper deleting a person's session rows, called from both the Employees page 'separate' action and from 'update' when an edit is what marks them as having left - the editor was the second way in and would otherwise have left them signed in.

nodes.label: session validation joins employee
nodes.rationale: validateSessionToken in src/lib/server/auth/session.ts inner joins employee (inner because user.employee_fk cannot be null) and deletes rather than merely refuses a session whose employee is not active, so the row does not sit until its eight-hour expiry.

nodes.label: SessionUser with nested employee object
nodes.rationale: Kept nested rather than flattened so it stays visible which table each field came from. hooks.server.ts builds this shape into locals.user, passing only the fields the app displays - birth date, sex and civil status stay on the server.

nodes.label: shared faceted filter and facet helpers
nodes.norm_label: shared faceted filter and facet helpers
nodes.rationale: The filter dropdown moved to src/lib/components/faceted-filter.svelte and its counting helpers to src/lib/utils/facets.ts once two tables needed them, rather than being written twice.

nodes.label: account_status (renamed from status)
nodes.rationale: active, inactive, locked. Renamed from the plain 'status' column so no word is shared between the two tables.

nodes.label: admin:view_employees and admin:manage_employees
nodes.rationale: A new 'employees' submodule under admin in PERMISSION_DEFS. Kept apart from admin:manage_users because creating a login and assigning a role decides who may do what system-wide, while correcting a spelling or recording a birth date does not. The Users page can still list employee names without admin:view_employees - that key controls opening the page, not reading names elsewhere.

nodes.label: employee table
nodes.rationale: One row per person in the office whether or not they log in, so that no signatory or staff record ever refers to a person the system does not know. Holds the identity facts - name parts, position title, org unit, birth date, sex, civil status, tenure status, employment status.

nodes.label: Employees page (/admin/employees)
nodes.rationale: Five columns - Name (with position underneath), Section, Tenure, Employment, Has login. Birthday, sex and civil status are edit-only because nobody scans a staff list for a birthday and they should not sit on screen for passers-by. Built as recommended rather than agreed, still open to change.

nodes.label: employment_status (active / separated)
nodes.rationale: Says whether the person still works here, separate from whether a login is active or locked. Still uncertain whether it needs finer values telling retirement, resignation and end of contract apart.

nodes.label: Organizational Structure page reads employee
nodes.rationale: org_unit_fk moved to employee, so the endpoint moved from [org_unit_pk]/users to [org_unit_pk]/employees and filters on employment_status. The delete guard had to move too - checking user would have let a populated division be deleted. Side effect - the list now includes people with no login, which is what the page always meant to show.

nodes.label: tenure_status (CSC hiring categories)
nodes.rationale: Seven values - permanent, temporary, casual, coterminous, contractual, cos, job_order. COS and Job Order are listed apart because those people are not government employees under Civil Service Commission rules but engaged under a separate joint circular. 'substitute' is excluded because the office never fills a post while its holder is on long leave; coterminous is a different idea, tied to a term or project rather than to an absent person.

nodes.label: user table (login only)
nodes.rationale: After the split the user row holds only sign-in facts - username, password hash, role_fk, account_status, must_change_password, failed_login_attempts, locked_until, last_login_at - because those are meaningless for a person who never signs in.

nodes.label: Users page (logins only)
nodes.rationale: Adding an account picks somebody already on the Employees page instead of typing a name; people who already have an account stay listed but unpickable so they do not read as missing. The person is locked when editing, because moving a login to another person is a new account, not an edit.

nodes.label: signatory history row
nodes.rationale: One row per version of a signatory's name and position title, with a date range saying when that version was in use. The date range belongs to the row, not the person, so overlapping ranges for one person are valid rather than an error.

nodes.label: signatory
nodes.rationale: A person whose name is printed on a report's signing line, not necessarily a system user. Kept as its own table rather than a flag on user, so someone like the PENR Officer who never logs in can still be a signatory and so a staff member leaving does not disturb the signatory history.

nodes.label: git feature flow
nodes.rationale: The whole workflow exists to control the shape of the graph on main - a short list of merge bubbles, one per feature, plus a few app-level commits, so `git log --graph` on main shows what landed and when without every intermediate commit.

nodes.label: EMS project context (CLAUDE.md)
nodes.rationale: Names the stack (SvelteKit, TypeScript with Svelte 5 runes, Tailwind, shadcn-svelte, Drizzle ORM, MySQL 8.4, adapter-node), the offline LAN constraint, and which documents to read before which kind of work.

nodes.label: employee_fk link on user
nodes.rationale: The link sits on user and is NOT NULL. A login always belongs to a person so the column is never empty there, while on employee it would be empty for most of the office. Required in the database rather than in application code so no code path can skip it and no screen needs a 'no person attached' branch. Confirmed that every account belongs to a real human - no service accounts.

nodes.label: 'Has login' column
nodes.rationale: The one column reaching across to the Users page. It answers the question the separation creates - who in this office still has no account - which would otherwise require opening both pages and comparing by hand.

nodes.label: no employee number column
nodes.rationale: The plantilla item number applies only to regular employees, so the column would be empty for the Contract of Service and Job Order part of the office.

nodes.label: one employee, one login
nodes.rationale: Enforced by the unique constraint user_employee_fk_unique. Two accounts for one human would make 'who changed this record?' ambiguous in the audit history. Different permissions are handled by changing the role, not by a second account.

nodes.label: position_title and tenure_status are required
nodes.rationale: The office hires a person into a named position, so a staff record with no position is not a real case; COS and JO staff hold no plantilla item but still hold a position or designation. They were optional at first only because they had been optional on the old user table. Consequence - create-admin.ts must write placeholders ('System Administrator', 'Permanent') and warn to correct the record afterwards.

nodes.label: role_fk stays on the login
nodes.rationale: 'Role' means two things - role in the office (position_title, on employee) and role in the app (a permission bundle, role_fk). On employee the app role would be empty for most of the office and every reader would first have to check whether the person has a login, a check that is easy to forget.

nodes.label: sign-in refuses anyone no longer employed
nodes.norm_label: sign-in refuses anyone no longer employed
nodes.rationale: Option C of three. Chosen over 'also switch the account off' because that leaves a gap - an admin could switch the account back on later without touching the employment record. The rule cannot be forgotten because it lives in the sign-in path. Accepted cost - the Users page must also show that the person has left, otherwise it reads 'Active' for an account that refuses to work.

nodes.label: three meanings of 'status' given distinct names
nodes.norm_label: three meanings of 'status' given distinct names
nodes.rationale: employment_status, civil_status, tenure_status on employee and account_status on user. The same word must never be reused for two different things across the two tables, otherwise a later query reads the wrong column. 'separated' unavoidably appears in two of them with different meanings, which is why the column names must stay distinct.

nodes.label: super-admin backfill in the permission sync
nodes.norm_label: super-admin backfill in the permission sync
nodes.rationale: scripts/sync-permissions.ts had three steps instead of the four the locked RBAC decisions require; re-normalizing does not help because nothing implies admin:manage_employees - implication runs upward only. The super-admin role is frozen and has no UI path to gain a module, so a missing key could only have been fixed by editing role_permission by hand. The added step finds the role by admin:manage_roles rather than by name, inserts what is missing in one transaction, names what it added, and skips gracefully on a fresh database. Staff keys are deliberately excluded.

nodes.label: two admin screens instead of one
nodes.norm_label: two admin screens instead of one
nodes.rationale: The combined dialog would ask for fourteen things; the two lists are different sizes (everyone vs only account holders); and the two jobs differ - clerical staff-list upkeep vs deciding who may do what. Accepted drawback - hiring someone who needs a login means visiting two pages. A 'Give this person a login' row action is a possible later improvement, recorded but not decided.

nodes.label: Topic 10 - full separation of employee and user
nodes.norm_label: topic 10 - full separation of employee and user
nodes.rationale: Chosen over 'employees only for non-users' (which scatters the office's people across two tables) and 'let user be the employee table' (which makes the login code responsible for always excluding password-less rows, easy to get wrong later). Recording every employee closes the Topic 3 gap where a signatory without an account had nothing to link to, and an employee list has value on its own. Cost - a real migration moving the name fields out of user, small at fewer than twenty users with no production data.

nodes.label: one person may hold several signatory rows at once
nodes.norm_label: one person may hold several signatory rows at once
nodes.rationale: The same person can be an active signatory under more than one position title simultaneously - for example Chief of the Environmental Management Division and OIC-PENR Officer - and the report preparer picks the right one.

nodes.label: no reports for periods before go-live
nodes.norm_label: no reports for periods before go-live
nodes.rationale: Only reports from go-live onward, so historical signatory assignments with past dates never need loading.

nodes.label: OIC needs no separate feature
nodes.rationale: The agency has no formal way of assigning an Officer-in-Charge - the next in rank signs informally - so a feature with start and end dates would mirror a process that does not exist. An OIC is just another signatory row with the acting title typed in and a date range, which the multiple-rows rule already supports.

nodes.label: reports reference a history row, not stored text
nodes.norm_label: reports reference a history row, not stored text
nodes.rationale: A typo and a real name change need opposite behaviour. Storing the name as text on each report freezes both alike, so a misspelling would be permanent across every record that used it and nobody would remember which records those were. With a foreign key to a history row, editing the row fixes a typo everywhere, while ending the row and creating a new one preserves old reports through a marriage or promotion. Consequence - the UI must offer 'Fix a spelling mistake' and 'This person's name changed' rather than a plain Edit button.

nodes.label: position title typed on the signatory row
nodes.norm_label: position title typed on the signatory row
nodes.rationale: Suggested from the person's record but never read live from it, because titles change with promotion or acting assignment and old reports must keep the title as it was printed.

nodes.label: fully offline LAN deployment
nodes.rationale: No internet dependency and no off-site access, which forces adapter-node over adapter-auto, bans CDN assets and fonts, and rules out OAuth or any third-party login in favour of session-based auth. Roughly 60% of clients are on WiFi, so session handling, form submissions and loading states must fail gracefully and recover rather than assume a stable link.

nodes.label: one role per user, no per-user overrides
nodes.norm_label: one role per user, no per-user overrides
nodes.rationale: Roles today are Admin, GSU (which approves other roles' requests), and per-section Encoder/Focal roles. Section-to-role mapping is still to be decided. Scale is under twenty users with five to ten concurrent.

nodes.label: deciding where a change belongs
nodes.rationale: Feature work goes on its feature branch; config, dependencies, tooling, docs and cross-cutting fixes go directly on main; a change touching several features goes as one honest mixed commit on main, because splitting it would create three half-merges and a tangled graph. When the bucket is unclear, ask rather than guess - guessing wrong means rewriting history.

nodes.label: stop and report on merge conflicts
nodes.norm_label: stop and report on merge conflicts
nodes.rationale: A conflict during main into feature usually means a real overlap the user needs to see, so never resolve by picking a side automatically and never abort silently.

nodes.label: leave merged feature branches alive
nodes.rationale: Branches here are long-lived - the user returns to a feature weeks later, merges main into it again and keeps going. Deleting merged branches is a common git reflex and is wrong in this repo.

nodes.label: merge asymmetry
nodes.rationale: feature into main is always --no-ff because the merge commit IS the record of the feature; main into feature is a plain merge where fast-forward is preferred, because bubbles inside a feature branch add noise. Rebase and squash are forbidden between these branches unless explicitly asked - both destroy the topology the workflow exists to preserve.

nodes.label: never push
nodes.rationale: Pushing is the user's last checkpoint before anything leaves the machine. Local commits and merges are fine; git fetch and other read-only remote commands are the one exception.

nodes.label: kebab-case files and conventional commit prefixes
nodes.norm_label: kebab-case files and conventional commit prefixes
nodes.rationale: Files and Svelte components use kebab-case; commits use a conventional prefix with a lowercase first letter; untracked or new files are feat:, never refactor:.

nodes.label: read the schema fresh before any query or migration
nodes.norm_label: read the schema fresh before any query or migration
nodes.rationale: src/lib/server/db/schema/index.ts must be re-read before writing a query, migration or table change; never work from a remembered copy - the employee/user separation is exactly the kind of change that invalidates a remembered schema.

nodes.label: EMS (Environmental Management System)
nodes.rationale: Tracks fuel, electricity, water and paper consumption plus ESWM and GHG compliance for DENR-PENRO Dinagat Islands, in support of ISO 14001:2015.

nodes.label: light HR flavour, not a personnel system
nodes.norm_label: light hr flavour, not a personnel system
nodes.rationale: Follow Civil Service Commission conventions where they exist so the fields feel familiar, but do not over-build. Leave records, payroll and service records are out of scope - this is an environmental management system.

nodes.label: DENR Official Seal (Department of Environment and Natural Resources, 1987)
nodes.norm_label: denr official seal (department of environment and natural resources, 1987)

nodes.label: Government Agency Identity of the EMS Deployment
nodes.norm_label: government agency identity of the ems deployment

nodes.label: Seal Iconography: Stylized Tree, Blue Sky, Green Terraced Land
nodes.norm_label: seal iconography: stylized tree, blue sky, green terraced land

nodes.label: Development Iconography Line Art (Wind Turbines, Solar Panels, Satellite, Cityscape, Circuitry, Heritage Buildings)
nodes.norm_label: development iconography line art (wind turbines, solar panels, satellite, cityscape, circuitry, heritage buildings)

nodes.label: Philippine Flag Motif (Eight-Rayed Sun and Three Stars)
nodes.norm_label: philippine flag motif (eight-rayed sun and three stars)

nodes.label: signatory conflict checker
nodes.rationale: Five candidate conflicts, none agreed - duplicate row, ambiguous suggestion, signatory whose account is gone, same person on two lines of one report (probably allowed, since the brief permits self-approval), and gap in coverage (arguably the most useful, since it blocks completing a report).

nodes.label: signatory roster
nodes.rationale: The list of who is currently expected to sign which line, used to suggest names when a report is made.

nodes.label: signing line / slot
